rv.q: The social satire is not biting enough, nor particularly pointed for our age, despite the updated look.
Once in a while, you find a production where every tiny detail gels together to create something wonderful – and The School for Scandal is the result.

But the resulting spectacle too often tries just a bit too hard, whether it’s in the heavily stylised line delivery, the neon lighting (Oliver Fenwick) or simply the over-the-top pinkness of it all – Lowde’s set is deliberately strident and makes no concession to subtlety.
But there’s so much style that the substance gets drowned out at times.
